# BTicino C300X Integration v2.8.0

## 2026-11-21

[![Support me on Ko-fi](https://ko-fi.com/img/githubbutton_sm.svg)](https://ko-fi.com/oliver7557)

## The C300X speaks

The device's own loudspeaker is now a media player in Home Assistant. Let it
say whatever your automations want to tell you at the door:

```yaml
action: tts.speak
target:
  entity_id: tts.piper
data:
  media_player_entity_id: media_player.bticino_c300x_speaker
  message: The washing machine is done.
```

- **Local:** the speech comes from the text-to-speech engine you choose. With
  Piper nothing leaves your network.
- **Spoken notifications:** the Notify action has a new `mode`: on the
  display as before, only spoken (`speech`), or shown and spoken instead of
  the tone (`both`). Choose the engine and language once under
  **Configure > Speech**.
- **The door comes first:** a ring or a call ends a sound at once, and no
  sound starts while a call is under way.
- Sounds from the media browser play too, with a volume and a stop.

The sound is telephone quality (8000 Hz), which is all the device plays.
Tested on firmware 1.7.19; firmware 2.0.2 and 3.0.6 have the same sound parts
but are not tested yet. Needs the agent update.

## Better camera picture

The camera picture can now be clearly better than from the factory. Under
**Configure > Camera quality** you choose:

- **Sharper:** up to 3000 kbit/s instead of 800.
- **Smoother:** up to 24 frames per second instead of 15. 25 is not offered,
  because the device then sends only about 8.
- **More picture:** the whole 720x576 camera picture instead of the factory
  688x480 cut-out. The size also applies to the camera picture on the C300X
  display and to answering-machine recordings.

The C300X reads these values only when it starts, so saving a change restarts
it once, which takes about a minute. The form shows the values saved on the
device and the ones it runs with. Removing the agent puts the original values
back. Needs the agent update.

On firmware 3.0.6 the area sets the low-resolution stream, the only one that
firmware sends, which the Door Entry app receives as well: sizes from 352x288
to 720x576, 100-2000 kbit/s and up to 25 frames per second. Sizes other than
the factory 400x288 are not tested on a 3.0.6 device yet.

## Display pages from the settings

Saving the settings with the display turned on under **Configure > Display**
now installs the Home Assistant pages on the C300X; turned off, it restores the
original display. Before, only the hidden **Display patch** switch did that.
The switch now saves the option too.
If your pages are missing after the update, open **Display and Display patch**
and submit it once.

## No SSH login to type in

Installing the agent, at setup and in the agent Repair, logs in with the C300X
factory root login. User and password are asked for only when the device
refuses it, for example after the root password was changed.

## Audio codec on firmware 3.0.6

The **Audio codec** select can now switch to **Speex** on firmware 3.0.6 too,
which comes with PCMU; it failed there before. This is not tested on a 3.0.6
device yet. Removing the agent puts back the codec the device came with.

## Tip: clearer sound with PCMU

If your C300X runs the factory Speex codec (firmware 1.7.19 and 2.0.2), set the **Audio codec**
select to **PCMU**. The browser plays PCMU as it is, so the agent no longer
converts the sound; that gives clearer audio and leaves the device more room.
Switching restarts the C300X once. The switch writes the same codec settings
BTicino itself ships on firmware 3.0.6, which already runs PCMU from the
factory.
